scope: Runtime companion, mock-only tests, and supplied test log. No study arm caches, outputs, or efficacy results read.

coverage_checked: only positions 116 through 119 accepted as the four pending exception keys
four pending entries restricted to original pending metadata and two complete source pairs
pending rows projected as unavailable without cache mutation or fabricated answer/telemetry
only 1080 unsent requests can proceed after the 120-position prefix
four-worker wave ordering and stop-after-drain behavior
new errors use a distinct stop file and preserve the existing stop file

review_findings.prefix_and_dispatch: Correctly binds all 1240 existing raw caches to originals plus the first 120 intervention positions; requires the four unavailable requests to equal dispatch positions 116-119 and leaves only the remaining 1080 unsent.
review_findings.pending_projection: Returns an explicit unavailable marker and null parsed answer using only recorded start time and timeout; does not write or resubmit the pending cache.
review_findings.no_fabrication: Does not add finish time, elapsed duration, return code, events, usage, or answer to the unknown attempt projection.
review_findings.paired_identity: Requires exactly two affected case IDs, each with one fresh and one repair request, and binds request/profile/source/feedback hashes.
review_findings.new_failure_policy: Drains one current four-request wave, writes a unique separate continuation stop record, then raises without dispatching later waves.
review_findings.namespace_and_live_gate: CLI is offline by default; live mode requires an explicit flag and an exact initial cache inventory, and notebook installation reuses embedded closures without external execution.

scope_limits: Actual amendment and request metadata preflight was not performed.
No live calls, cache mutations, cache reads, or outcome inspection occurred.
The overlay's explicit interruption marker is carried in `transport_error`; it must be labeled as controller interruption/outcome unavailable, not a model or provider failure.
